prompt.brief: Design Twitter for millions of users: people can publish short posts, follow accounts, read a home timeline, and see new posts appear without overwhelming the system when popular users publish.
successSignals: Separate the durable post and follow graph from the read-optimized home timeline projection.
Choose a fanout strategy based on follower count and make celebrity posts safe for hot keys and burst traffic.
Define cursor pagination, ordering, deletion, privacy, and idempotency instead of treating the feed as an unbounded list.
Keep media processing, search, analytics, and notifications asynchronous so timeline reads and writes remain predictable.

functional: Allow authenticated users to publish, delete, and read short text posts with optional media references.
Allow users to follow and unfollow accounts, then read a reverse-chronological home timeline.
Show a user's profile timeline and a post detail view with replies, reposts, and likes as extensible interactions.
Refresh the home timeline and notify clients when new posts are available, subject to visibility and moderation rules.
nonFunctional: Target p95 under 200 ms for a timeline page read and under 150 ms for publishing metadata before asynchronous work.
A committed post must be durable and eventually visible to eligible followers; brief feed lag is acceptable and observable.
Support privacy, blocked users, deleted content, abuse controls, rate limits, and authenticated access at every read path.
Remain available during celebrity-post bursts, regional failures, slow media processing, and partial fanout backlog.
scaleAssumptions: 500 million registered users, 100 million daily active users, and 50 million posts per day.
Assume 20 timeline reads per daily active user and 10x traffic bursts around major events.
Most users follow fewer than 1,000 accounts; a small set of accounts has tens of millions of followers.
Keep post metadata in a durable partitioned store, media in object storage, and feed entries as rebuildable projections with a retention window.

metrics.label: Post rate
metrics.description: 50M daily posts with burst capacity for live events and retry storms.

metrics.label: Timeline reads
metrics.description: 100M daily users at 20 reads each; cache and precomputed entries absorb hot reads.

metrics.label: Read latency
metrics.description: Fetch a bounded page by cursor without scanning the entire follow graph.

metrics.label: Feed freshness
metrics.description: Normal fanout target; show a refresh affordance when stream or projection lag grows.

dataFlow.title: Publish a post
dataFlow.description: The post service authenticates the author, validates content and visibility, writes the post and moderation state, and returns the durable version.

dataFlow.title: Update the follow graph
dataFlow.description: Follow edges are conditionally updated and emit graph events that determine future fanout and timeline authorization.

dataFlow.title: Fan out ordinary posts
dataFlow.description: Workers push post IDs to follower timeline partitions, coalescing retries and isolating authors with large follower counts.

dataFlow.title: Read the home timeline
dataFlow.description: The timeline service merges pushed entries with pull-time candidates for high-follower authors, ranks them, and returns a cursor.

dataFlow.title: Broadcast and repair live updates
dataFlow.description: Live gateways send new-post IDs with cursors; clients resync from the timeline when connections or projections fall behind.

architecture.title: Twitter-style home timeline reference architecture
architecture.summary: Durable posts and follow edges feed a hybrid timeline pipeline: push fanout serves ordinary accounts, while pull-on-read protects the system from celebrity fanout explosions.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Clients publish posts, read cursor-paginated feeds, and receive freshness-aware refresh events.

layers.label: Source and control plane
layers.description: Post and graph services own durable content, relationships, authorization, and moderation state.

layers.label: Feed and event plane
layers.description: Events are partitioned, fanout is hybrid, and timeline projections are independently rebuilt and cached.

layers.label: Asynchronous extensions
layers.description: Media, search, notifications, analytics, and repair consume events without blocking the core feed path.

keyPaths.label: Publish path
keyPaths.description: Client -> edge -> post service -> durable post store -> event stream.

keyPaths.label: Home timeline path
keyPaths.description: Timeline request -> cache/store, merged with hot-author pull results and visibility checks.

keyPaths.label: Hybrid fanout path
keyPaths.description: Feed event -> strategy -> push projection or pull-on-read for high-follower authors.

components.label: Web and mobile clients
components.description: Publish posts, request bounded feed pages, and subscribe for new-post notifications.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Terminates TLS, authenticates users, applies quotas, and routes by user or post key.

components.label: Post service
components.description: Validates, authorizes, stores, and deletes posts while emitting durable publication events.

components.label: Post store
components.description: Partitioned durable source of truth for post metadata, visibility, and moderation state.

components.label: Social graph service
components.description: Manages follow edges, blocks, privacy, and recipient lookups with versioned changes.

components.label: Follow graph
components.description: Durable adjacency lists optimized for follower enumeration and relationship checks.

components.label: Feed event stream
components.description: Retained, partitioned events for fanout, indexing, notifications, analytics, and replay.

components.label: Hybrid fanout service
components.description: Chooses push, pull, or hybrid delivery from follower count, backlog, and account policy.

components.label: Timeline projections
components.description: Sharded, rebuildable feed entries keyed by recipient with cursor-friendly rank keys.

components.label: Feed cache
components.description: Caches recent pages and post summaries with version or lag metadata to absorb read bursts.

components.label: Timeline service
components.description: Reads projections, merges pull sources for hot authors, filters visibility, and creates opaque cursors.

components.label: Live update gateway
components.description: Tracks feed subscribers and coalesces new-post notifications; clients fetch the authoritative page on refresh.

components.label: Media pipeline
components.description: Scans, resizes, and publishes media through object storage and a CDN without blocking post metadata.

components.label: Search index
components.description: Indexes eligible posts and accounts asynchronously for discovery and search queries.

components.label: Notification service
components.description: Delivers mentions, follows, and selected post notifications with dedupe and provider retries.

components.label: Analytics and abuse
components.description: Consumes events for trends, ranking signals, abuse detection, and product reporting.

components.label: Design Twitter monitoring
components.description: Tracks feed lag, fanout backlog, cache hit rate, hot partitions, read latency, and projection drift.

connections.description: Serves recent pages while preserving freshness metadata.

deepDives.title: Hybrid fanout for celebrity authors
points: For Twitter's post, follow, home-timeline, and live-update platform, post publication is durable before fanout, and every timeline item remains subject to current visibility and graph policy.
Design for the failure case where celebrity posts, unfollows, deletes, and reconnect storms must not cause write amplification or stale exposure; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Timeline pagination and ranking
points: For Twitter's post, follow, home-timeline, and live-update platform, post publication is durable before fanout, and every timeline item remains subject to current visibility and graph policy.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by Twitter's post, follow, home-timeline, and live-update platform access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Fanout-on-write versus fanout-on-read
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use hybrid fanout: push to ordinary followers and pull high-fanout authors at read time.
tradeoffs.caution: Pure write fanout explodes for celebrities; pure read fanout makes home timelines too slow.

tradeoffs.title: Precomputed timeline versus ranked query
tradeoffs.recommendation: Store candidate timeline entries and perform bounded ranking/merge on read with cursor state.
tradeoffs.caution: A fully materialized ranked feed is expensive to invalidate whenever follows or ranking rules change.

tradeoffs.title: Live push versus reliable pull
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push low-latency post IDs with a cursor, but make timeline reads the recovery path.
tradeoffs.caution: Sockets disconnect; treating push as guaranteed loses posts.

commonMistakes: Fanout to every follower synchronously with post creation.
Using offset pagination while the timeline changes rapidly.
Leaving deleted or unfollowed posts in cached timelines.
Using follower count as the only hot-key strategy.
Having no cursor/resync path for live updates.

followUps.question: How do you publish for a celebrity account?
followUps.answer: Store the post once, use pull-time candidate injection or bounded hybrid fanout, and isolate live subscribers from ordinary writes.

followUps.question: What if a user unfollows immediately after a post is fanned out?
followUps.answer: Keep graph/visibility checks at read time, invalidate entries asynchronously, and treat the edge version as part of the timeline generation.

followUps.question: How do you avoid missing posts during reconnect?
followUps.answer: Persist a live cursor, replay from the event watermark when retained, and fall back to a timeline snapshot with deduplicated post IDs.

rubric.description: The answer defines post durability, graph versioning, hybrid fanout, timeline cursors, ranking, visibility, hot authors, and live resync, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make Twitter's post, follow, home-timeline, and live-update platform state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the Twitter's post, follow, home-timeline, and live-update platform consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
